Findings marked verified-present/verified-absent were decided against the installed QNX SDP 8.0 (build 8.0.0.00141T202311271501L) by header, symbol and qcc compile/link probes; nothing was run on a QNX target. All other findings keep their known/guess label: 'guess' is an unverified claim about QNX 8.0.

findings.title: Raw Linux syscall()
findings.message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX, and syscall() is not declared in the SDP (build 141). gettid() DOES exist natively (declared in <sys/process.h>, exported by libc), so SYS_gettid callers need only the call. [verified on SDP 8.0.0.00141T202311271501L by compile/link probe, not run on target: syscall: found only in io-sock kernel/driver headers (devs/), not in any user-facing header; compile probe fails]
findings.remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps. gettid(): include <sys/process.h> and call gettid() (present; whether the number is a Linux-style kernel tid was not checked: use it as a numeric id for logging, not for kernel interfaces). Do not substitute pthread_self() (opaque handle). futex has no mechanical replacement (not declared; no library exports it): redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
findings.verify: checked against the installed SDP (header, symbol and qcc probes); not executed on a QNX target.

items.evidence: syscall: found only in io-sock kernel/driver headers (devs/), not in any user-facing header; compile probe fails

findings.title: Includes a Linux-specific <sys/...> header
findings.message: This glibc/Linux <sys/...> header is not in the QNX 8.0 SDP for most of the names this rule matches (sys/epoll.h, eventfd.h, signalfd.h, timerfd.h, prctl.h, sendfile.h, sysinfo.h, fanotify.h do not exist in build 141). Two exceptions are present: <sys/inotify.h> (needs -lfsnotify) and <sys/auxv.h> (exists, but getauxval is not declared). [verified on SDP 8.0.0.00141T202311271501L by compile/link probe, not run on target: <sys/prctl.h> not found / does not compile with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le]
findings.remedy: Remove the include together with the calls it supports (see the per-API findings), or guard it with #if defined(__linux__) and add a __QNXNTO__ branch.
findings.verify: checked against the installed SDP (header, symbol and qcc probes); not executed on a QNX target.

items.evidence: <sys/prctl.h> not found / does not compile with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le

findings.title: Includes a Linux kernel header
findings.message: <linux/...> and <asm/...> are Linux kernel uapi headers. The QNX SDP 8.0 (build 141) ships no linux/, asm/ or asm-generic/ directory: every such include fails to compile (checked for 21 common ones with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le). Many uses are trivial (linux/limits.h, linux/types.h can be replaced by POSIX headers); device-ioctl headers are not. [verified on SDP 8.0.0.00141T202311271501L by compile/link probe, not run on target: <linux/types.h> not found / does not compile with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le]
findings.remedy: Replace each use with the POSIX/QNX equivalent of what the header supplied (types, constants). If it is a device ioctl header, the device needs a QNX resource-manager interface (devctl) instead.
findings.verify: checked against the installed SDP (header, symbol and qcc probes); not executed on a QNX target.

items.evidence: <linux/types.h> not found / does not compile with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le

findings.title: prctl

context.text: Failure doesn't really matter, it's mostly aesthetic */

findings.message: prctl is a Linux process-control multiplexer. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/prctl.h>, no prctl symbol, no PR_* macro in SDP 8.0 build 141). [verified on SDP 8.0.0.00141T202311271501L by compile/link probe, not run on target: PR_SET_NAME: not declared in any user header of the SDP and not exported by any SDP library; probe: #error PR_SET_NAME not defined]
findings.remedy: Map each option individually: PR_SET_NAME -> pthread_setname_np() (declared and exported in SDP 8.0 build 141; so is pthread_getname_np); PR_SET_PDEATHSIG -> a parent-liveness check; PR_SET_DUMPABLE/NO_NEW_PRIVS -> drop (no QNX analogue is known).
findings.verify: checked against the installed SDP (header, symbol and qcc probes); not executed on a QNX target.

findings.title: getrandom
findings.message: getrandom is a Linux syscall wrapper. On SDP 8.0 build 141 getrandom is not declared and GRND_* do not exist; getentropy is not declared either (an unrelated library, libunbound, exports a private symbol of that name, so a call without a prototype would link to the wrong thing). arc4random is not available to user code. [verified on SDP 8.0.0.00141T202311271501L by compile/link probe, not run on target: getrandom: not declared in any user header of the SDP and not exported by any SDP library; probe: 'getrandom' undeclared (first use in this function); did you mean 'srandom'?]
findings.remedy: Read from /dev/urandom (QNX provides it; a helper that handles short reads and EINTR is enough). <entropy.h> in the SDP is the QNX entropy-source interface (entropy_return_status/entropy_sleep exist in the header; entropy_return_status does not link by default), not a getrandom replacement.
findings.verify: checked against the installed SDP (header, symbol and qcc probes); not executed on a QNX target.

findings.title: Makefile branches on uname
findings.message: Platform is taken from the build host. When cross-compiling the host is Linux/macOS while the target is QNX; uname on a QNX host reports QNX.
findings.remedy: Key the logic on a target variable (for example TARGET_OS passed on the command line) rather than uname of the build machine.

findings.title: Linux-specific socket options

context.text: if(interface && setsockopt(sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BINDTODEVICE, interface, strlen(interface)) < 0) {
TRACE(("Failed setsockopt with errno failure, %d %s", errno, strerror(errno)))

findings.message: Socket options that originated on Linux. On SDP 8.0 build 141: TCP_FASTOPEN, TCP_INFO, TCP_NODELAY, TCP_KEEPIDLE/INTVL/CNT, SO_REUSEPORT are defined; TCP_CORK, TCP_QUICKACK, TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT, TCP_USER_TIMEOUT, MSG_MORE, SO_BINDTODEVICE, SO_PRIORITY, SO_MARK, IP_PKTINFO-style Linux options are not. [verified on SDP 8.0.0.00141T202311271501L by compile/link probe, not run on target: SO_BINDTODEVICE: not declared in any user header of the SDP and not exported by any SDP library; probe: #error SO_BINDTODEVICE not defined]
findings.remedy: Guard each setsockopt/getsockopt with #ifdef so it compiles away when the macro is undefined. Where the macro IS defined (TCP_INFO, TCP_FASTOPEN, SO_REUSEPORT) the struct layout and semantics are BSD's and were not tested: confirm before relying on a same-named constant.
findings.verify: checked against the installed SDP (header, symbol and qcc probes); not executed on a QNX target.

findings.title: Autotools project with no QNX host support
findings.message: No QNX mention in the tree. Old bundled config.sub/config.guess may not recognise a QNX host triplet.
findings.remedy: Refresh config.sub/config.guess (autoreconf -fi or copy from a current automake), then configure with --host=<cpu>-unknown-nto-qnx<version> and CC set to qcc.
findings.verify: verify against SDP: exact host triplet format for 8.0.

rules.remedy: Refresh config.sub/config.guess (autoreconf -fi or copy from a current automake), then configure with --host=<cpu>-unknown-nto-qnx<version> and CC set to qcc.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: exact host triplet format for 8.0.
rules.message: No QNX mention in the tree. Old bundled config.sub/config.guess may not recognise a QNX host triplet.

rules.title: Makefile branches on uname
rules.remedy: Key the logic on a target variable (for example TARGET_OS passed on the command line) rather than uname of the build machine.
rules.message: Platform is taken from the build host. When cross-compiling the host is Linux/macOS while the target is QNX; uname on a QNX host reports QNX.

rules.title: Includes a Linux kernel header
rules.remedy: Replace each use with the POSIX/QNX equivalent of what the header supplied (types, constants). If it is a device ioctl header, the device needs a QNX resource-manager interface (devctl) instead.
rules.verify: Checked on SDP 8.0 build 141: no linux/ or asm/ include directory exists. Other SDP versions: verify against SDP.
rules.message: <linux/...> and <asm/...> are Linux kernel uapi headers. The QNX SDP 8.0 (build 141) ships no linux/, asm/ or asm-generic/ directory: every such include fails to compile (checked for 21 common ones with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le). Many uses are trivial (linux/limits.h, linux/types.h can be replaced by POSIX headers); device-ioctl headers are not.

rules.title: Includes a Linux-specific <sys/...> header
rules.remedy: Remove the include together with the calls it supports (see the per-API findings), or guard it with #if defined(__linux__) and add a __QNXNTO__ branch.
rules.verify: Per-header result from SDP 8.0 build 141 (qcc include probe). Other SDP versions: verify against SDP.
rules.message: This glibc/Linux <sys/...> header is not in the QNX 8.0 SDP for most of the names this rule matches (sys/epoll.h, eventfd.h, signalfd.h, timerfd.h, prctl.h, sendfile.h, sysinfo.h, fanotify.h do not exist in build 141). Two exceptions are present: <sys/inotify.h> (needs -lfsnotify) and <sys/auxv.h> (exists, but getauxval is not declared).

rules.title: prctl
rules.remedy: Map each option individually: PR_SET_NAME -> pthread_setname_np() (declared and exported in SDP 8.0 build 141; so is pthread_getname_np); PR_SET_PDEATHSIG -> a parent-liveness check; PR_SET_DUMPABLE/NO_NEW_PRIVS -> drop (no QNX analogue is known).
rules.verify: Absence and pthread_setname_np verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); argument limits of pthread_setname_np not checked.
rules.message: prctl is a Linux process-control multiplexer. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/prctl.h>, no prctl symbol, no PR_* macro in SDP 8.0 build 141).

rules.title: getrandom
rules.remedy: Read from /dev/urandom (QNX provides it; a helper that handles short reads and EINTR is enough). <entropy.h> in the SDP is the QNX entropy-source interface (entropy_return_status/entropy_sleep exist in the header; entropy_return_status does not link by default), not a getrandom replacement.
rules.verify: Absence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; /dev/urandom exists on the target image: not checked here.
rules.message: getrandom is a Linux syscall wrapper. On SDP 8.0 build 141 getrandom is not declared and GRND_* do not exist; getentropy is not declared either (an unrelated library, libunbound, exports a private symbol of that name, so a call without a prototype would link to the wrong thing). arc4random is not available to user code.

rules.title: Raw Linux syscall()
rules.remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps. gettid(): include <sys/process.h> and call gettid() (present; whether the number is a Linux-style kernel tid was not checked: use it as a numeric id for logging, not for kernel interfaces). Do not substitute pthread_self() (opaque handle). futex has no mechanical replacement (not declared; no library exports it): redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
rules.verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141: syscall and futex absent, gettid present.
rules.message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX, and syscall() is not declared in the SDP (build 141). gettid() DOES exist natively (declared in <sys/process.h>, exported by libc), so SYS_gettid callers need only the call.

rules.title: Linux-specific socket options
rules.remedy: Guard each setsockopt/getsockopt with #ifdef so it compiles away when the macro is undefined. Where the macro IS defined (TCP_INFO, TCP_FASTOPEN, SO_REUSEPORT) the struct layout and semantics are BSD's and were not tested: confirm before relying on a same-named constant.
rules.verify: Macro presence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (compile probe); semantics not run.
rules.message: Socket options that originated on Linux. On SDP 8.0 build 141: TCP_FASTOPEN, TCP_INFO, TCP_NODELAY, TCP_KEEPIDLE/INTVL/CNT, SO_REUSEPORT are defined; TCP_CORK, TCP_QUICKACK, TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT, TCP_USER_TIMEOUT, MSG_MORE, SO_BINDTODEVICE, SO_PRIORITY, SO_MARK, IP_PKTINFO-style Linux options are not.

rules.title: Linux-only preprocessor branch without QNX branch
rules.remedy: Add an explicit #elif defined(__QNXNTO__) branch, or widen the condition if the code is POSIX-generic.
rules.message: A Linux conditional on this line does not mention QNX. QNX compilers predefine __QNXNTO__ (and __QNX__).

rules.title: UNIX-domain socket IPC
rules.remedy: First port as-is. If this is a hot request/reply path, consider ChannelCreate()/MsgSend()/MsgReceive()/MsgReply(); it gives priority inheritance across the call.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: abstract-namespace sockets (leading NUL in sun_path) are Linux-only.
rules.message: Likely works unchanged (POSIX), listed because request/reply IPC is where QNX native message passing pays off.

rules.title: Linux /proc paths
rules.remedy: Replace with POSIX/QNX queries: sysconf(), getrusage(), the system page (<sys/syspage.h>) for CPU/memory facts, procfs ioctls (DCMD_PROC_*) for process info.
rules.verify: verify against SDP: procfs layout on QNX 8.0.
rules.message: QNX has a /proc, but it is a different interface (process address spaces, not Linux text files).
